text:
sam: heads up — evaluating marengo-9b (community release). License text attached in model repo looks like CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 + extra attribution file. can we put this on hosted API for customers to use?
ida: NC = non-commercial, so that rules out commercial hosting/paid access. need to see exact wording in the repo, but likely not allowed for paid API.
priya: quick context — latencies look good, quantized INT8 gives ~2.2x throughput. team wants to run internal benchmarks and a small canary with internal users. is that permitted?
ida: internal research/eval is typically fine under NC, as long as not used to provide a commercial service. internal benchmarks for model quality are okay.
sam: what about offering it under Hosted but gated as "research preview" (free, invite-only)? customers still sign up via our product; does that count as commercial?
ida: if there's no payment and it's explicitly research-only with TOS restricting commercial productization, that's a grey area. we should avoid exposing it to external users via paid endpoints. free demos to vetted academic partners might be OK after a legal review and explicit agreement.
legal-bot: AUTO: please attach the model LICENSE and any third-party data provenance files. See playbook: /docs/legal/model-licenses for criteria.
oliver: question — for Dedicated (reserved capacity) where customer self-pays for infra — could we let them bring marengo-9b as a hosted model within their dedicated pool?
ida: Dedicated where the customer controls the model is effectively self-hosted for them. If the customer supplies the model and accepts the license terms, that can be okay. But if we distribute the model binary to their environment (e.g., we export quantized weights), that's redistribution and may violate NC-SA. Need to confirm whether the license allows distribution to customers' infra.
priya: technical detail — our quantization pipeline produces an ".qw" file and we currently store cached quantized weights in S3 for fast rollout. If the license forbids redistribution, we can't share the .qw outside our legal boundary.
ida: correct — redistributed derivatives (including quantized weights) are likely considered derivative works under CC-SA. Sharing them to customers is redistribution; hosting them ourselves in hosted infra for commercial endpoints would also be problematic.
sam: could we host the full model but enforce a usage filter that blocks commercial endpoints (e.g., block API keys tied to paying orgs)?
ida: enforcement is hard and risky. Licensing doesn't hinge on billing alone — offering access that enables commercial use could violate NC. We'd need a legal-safe gating mechanism and explicit downstream usage terms plus logs/audit. Still prefer not to put NC models on paid Hosted.
priya: for internal canary and eval bench, i'll run quantization locally and keep artifacts in a restricted research bucket. no outbound distribution.
oliver: what about converting to embeddings-only endpoint? sometimes models' embeddings are allowed while generation is restricted?
ida: embeddings do not change the underlying license — the model is still being used to produce embeddings. If the license restricts commercial use of the model, using it to power a commercial embeddings feature is still a violation. Need explicit permission from authors.
sam: ok. action items: 1) priya will run internal INT8 evals and keep artifacts in research-only S3. 2) ida to request clarification from model authors on commercial carveouts and redistribution of quantized weights. 3) legal-bot to create a tracker ticket.
priya: I'll also export a small benchmark (diffed outputs) and share in private research slack thread, no binaries.
ida: if authors grant a commercial license or dual-license, we can revisit hosting. until then, treat marengo-9b as research-only.
legal-bot: AUTO: created ticket LEGAL-ML-482 for marengo-9b license clarification.
sam: thanks all. tagging @oliver to keep product in the loop for blocked onboarding. :thumbsup:
